about.title: Oakland Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A wet produce aisle in Fruitvale, a broken stair rail in an East Oakland apartment building, a buckled sidewalk outside a storefront on International Boulevard — falls in Oakland rarely happen on open, well-kept ground. They happen where somebody was responsible for keeping things safe and didn't. Under California law, that responsibility is the heart of a premises liability claim. You generally need to show the owner or manager knew about the hazard, or reasonably should have, and failed to repair it or warn you. That is why what you do in the first days matters so much: photograph the spot, note the time, get the names of anyone who saw it, and ask that surveillance footage be saved before it is overwritten. California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly distracted, a claim can still move forward. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Oakland residents, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Oakland Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice is the whole case
items.desc: California requires proof that the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know how to dig for cleaning logs, prior complaints, and inspection records that show how long a problem was ignored.

items.title: Video disappears fast
items.desc: Many Oakland businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting an attorney involved early means a preservation letter goes out before the most useful evidence is gone.

items.title: Deadlines aren't all the same
items.desc: You generally have two years to file against a private owner, but a claim involving City of Oakland or other public property has a much shorter government claim window. An attorney sorts out who owns the property and which clock applies.

items.question: I tripped on a broken sidewalk in Oakland. Is the city responsible or the property owner?
items.answer: It depends on who controls that stretch of sidewalk and what caused the defect, and the answer is not always obvious. When a public entity like the City of Oakland or Alameda County may be involved, California requires a government claim to be filed within a much shorter window — generally six months — before a lawsuit can proceed. Because of that, it's worth having an attorney identify the responsible party quickly rather than assuming you have two years.

items.question: The store says I wasn't watching where I was going. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: No. California uses pure comparative fault, which means your recovery may be reduced by your share of responsibility but is not eliminated. The store still has to answer for whether it knew about the hazard, or should have, and failed to fix or warn about it. An attorney can push back on the argument that you were solely to blame.

items.question: Does it cost anything to be connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we don't charge you for the connection. The independent attorneys in our network handle premises liability cases on contingency, so there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
